case.equipment: PNP proximity sensor, Allen-Bradley Micro820 PLC, 24 VDC I/O
case.question: Proximity sensor on pump discharge is PNP type, wired to a 24 DC input on the Micro820. Sensor is not triggering the input even though the object is in range. What should you verify?

key_points: PNP sensor switches to +24V (supply/high) when triggered; NPN switches to ground (common)
PNP output can drive an input if sensor common and input common are the same reference; if isolated, wiring will fail
Verify: sensor supply voltage, sensor common connected to input common, input voltage reading with object present
wrong_if: Blames the sensor without checking wiring or power supply
Confuses PNP (switches to +V/supply) with NPN (switches to ground/common)
Assumes the input is broken without testing voltage at the input terminal

turns.question: Proximity sensor on pump discharge is PNP type, wired to a 24 DC input on the Micro820. Sensor is not triggering the input even though the object is in range. What should you verify?
turns.answer:
The first thing to check is that the sensor actually has 24 V DC present at its supply leads.  

1. Verify the 24 VDC supply is on and correctly connected to the sensor’s power pins (measure voltage with a multimeter).  
2. Confirm the sensor’s output wiring: PNP devices source the input when active, so the Micro820 input should be tied to the sensor’s positive output and the input’s negative side to common/ground.  
3. Check that the Micro820 input module is configured for a sourcing (PNP) signal and that the input is enabled in the PLC program.  
4. Inspect the sensor’s LED (if any) for status; a steady or blinking LED often indicates proper power but no detection.  
5. Measure the sensor’s output voltage while the target is in range – you should see the voltage rise to near 24 V when the object is present.  
6. Ensure the sensor’s sensing distance and alignment are correct for the object; clean the sensing face of any dirt or coating.  

*Is the 24 VDC actually present at the sensor terminals when the system is powered?*
